title: Smooth morphisms satisfy the preservation clauses
statement:
In the purity conventions of this chapter ([def-pur-conventions] fixed setting),
let $X,Y$ be finite-type $k$-schemes [def-weil-finite-type-morphism],
and let $f:X\to Y$ be a smooth separated finite-type $k$-morphism
of pure relative dimension $d\geq0$. Here $Rf^!$ denotes the
constructible exceptional functor of [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image].
The
ambient exceptional right
adjoint datum of [def-weil-ambient-exceptional-adjoint] was the
hypothesis under which this corollary was formerly stated; it is not assumed
here, being on the bounded constructible and finite-Tor coefficients that the
two clauses below quantify over the theorem
[cor-sf-ambient-adjoint-discharge]. Then $f$ satisfies the
two preservation clauses of
[def-weil-exceptional-adjoint-admissibility], with
$c_f^-=c_f^+=-2d$ in the signed convention of that definition:

1. *constructibility.* For all integers $a\leq b$,
$$
L\in D_c^{[a,b]}(Y,A)\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
Rf^!L\in D_c^{[a-2d,b-2d]}(X,A).
$$
1. *finite Tor amplitude.* If $K\in D^b_{ctf}(Y,A)$ has
finite Tor amplitude in
$[a,b]$, then $Rf^!K$ has finite Tor amplitude in
$[a-2d,b-2d]$; in particular $Rf^!$ carries $D^b_{ctf}(Y,A)$
into $D^b_{ctf}(X,A)$.

Thus every such smooth morphism is
exceptional-adjoint admissible at $A=A_{E,n}$ in the constructible sense —
the three clauses of [def-weil-exceptional-adjoint-admissibility] read on the
complexes of the blueprint's coefficient class that the two clauses above
quantify over; the unrestricted clause (1) of that definition, on all
pro-etale sheaves, is false in general and is not asserted —: the
preservation
clauses are consequences of purity, not hypotheses of it, and the ambient
datum that the earlier form of this corollary assumed is not an assumption
either, by [cor-sf-ambient-adjoint-discharge]. The further statement
``admissible at $\Lambda\in\{\mathcal O_E,E,\Qlb\}$'' demands in addition the
uniformity of the two clauses over the finite stages and the
finite-reduction and scalar-extension compatibilities of the right adjoints;
those are the coefficient transport of the transport section at the end of
this chapter, and they are *not* asserted here.

proof.text: Check the geometric hypotheses of the ordinary etale purity theorem. The base $\operatorname{Spec}k$ is Noetherian, since a field has only the ideals $0$ and $k$. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian], $X$ and $Y$ are Noetherian; in particular $Y$ is quasi-compact. By [lem-weil-pbc-locally-noetherian-quasi-separated], $Y$ is quasi-separated. Apply [thm-nagata-compactification] to the separated finite-type $f$ to choose a compactification. For the coefficient data of [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension], [lem-weil-l-adic-extension-integers-dvr] makes $\mathcal O_E$ a DVR with finite residue field. Then [lem-weil-valued-dvr-finite-quotients] makes $A=A_{E,n}$ finite. Since $|\ell|_E=|\ell|_\ell<1$, one has $\ell\in\mathfrak m_E=(\varpi_E)$, hence $\ell^n\in(\varpi_E^n)$ and $N=\ell^n$ kills $A$. This $N$ is invertible on the $k$-scheme $Y$, since $\ell\ne p$. Thus $Y$, $f$, $A$ and $d$ satisfy precisely the Noetherian-base, compactifiability, exponent and pure-relative-dimension hypotheses of [thm-asd-smooth-tensor].

source.place: Proof, opening use of ordinary etale smooth tensor duality; hypotheses made explicit

proof.text:
For any $M\in D^b_c(Y,A)$, choose $G\in D^b_c(Y_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ and $M\cong
u_Y^*G$ using [lem-sf-proetale-constructible-origin](ii). Exactness and the cohomology formula of [lem-sf-comparison-pullback-exact] give $\mathcal H^r(M)\cong
u_Y^*\mathcal H^r(G)$. The equivalence on constructible sheaves in [lem-sf-proetale-constructible-origin](i) reflects zero objects, so $G$ has exactly the same cohomological vanishing interval as $M$. Use the formula on etale-origin inputs in [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image] to write
$$Rf^!M\cong
u_X^*f^	imes G.$$
The bounded-class adjunction is supplied by [cor-sf-ambient-adjoint-discharge]. This invokes no unrestricted pro-etale ambient adjunction and does not use preservation of constructibility by $f^!$ as a hypothesis.

source.place: Proof, opening comparison to ordinary etale coefficients; replaces the incorrect compact-support base-change citation

proof.text:
Put $\omega_f=f^\times A_Y$. By [thm-asd-smooth-tensor], there is a sheaf $T$ of $A_X$-modules, locally constant and locally free of rank one, and an isomorphism $\omega_f\cong T[2d]$. For every ordinary etale complex $G$, including a bounded constructible complex that has no finite Tor amplitude, that same theorem gives
$$f^\times G\cong f^{-1}G\otimes_A^L\omega_f.$$
Choose an etale covering family $u_i:U_i\to X$ trivializing $T$. The numerical preservation statements require the rank-one local trivializations, and do not require a choice of the canonical Tate orientation.

source.place: Proof, opening assertion for bounded constructible inputs without finite Tor amplitude; unit step (iii), purity

proof.text:
For each $u=u_i$, apply [lem-kun-inverse-image-monoidal] to the tensor formula and use that the exact module inverse image in [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact] is termwise on complexes. It takes $T[2d]$ to $A_U[2d]$. Since derived tensor is triangulated in its second variable by [lem-kun-derived-tensor-triangulated], this gives
$$u^{-1}f^\times G\cong (u^{-1}f^{-1}G)\otimes_A^L A_U[2d]\cong (u^{-1}f^{-1}G)[2d].$$
The last unit isomorphism is computed by $P\otimes_A A_U=P$ for a K-flat representative $P$, using [def-kun-derived-tensor]. The displayed local formula holds for every $G$; finite Tor amplitude has not been used.

source.place: Proof, constructibility calculation: local expansion of the purity tensor formula

proof.text:
Let $M\in D_c^{[a,b]}(Y,A)$ and use its $G$ from step 2. By [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact] and [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-bounded-below], $\mathcal H^r(f^{-1}G)\cong f^{-1}\mathcal H^r(G)$; the same cohomology formula holds for restriction by $u_i^{-1}$. Each $f^{-1}\mathcal H^r(G)$ is constructible by [prop-constructible-pullback], applied to its underlying sheaf; the induced module action is the action in the module inverse-image theorem. On the pulled-back strata, local trivializations as finite constant $A$-modules remain such by [lem-kun-pullback-constant], so this is constructibility as $A$-modules, not merely as underlying sets. The local formula of step 4 and [lem-sp-derived-cohomology-shift] yield
$$u_i^{-1}\mathcal H^r(f^\times G)\cong u_i^{-1}f^{-1}\mathcal H^{r+2d}(G).$$
For $r\notin[a-2d,b-2d]$ the right side is zero, hence the left sides vanish on a covering and $\mathcal H^r(f^\times G)=0$. For each of the finitely many remaining $r$, take a finite constructible stratification for $f^{-1}\mathcal H^{r+2d}(G)$. For a stratum $Z\hookrightarrow X$, write $v_i:Z\times_XU_i\to Z$ for the pulled-back etale cover and $F_Z=(f^{-1}\mathcal H^{r+2d}(G))|_Z$. Restricting the displayed cohomology isomorphism to $Z\times_XU_i$ gives $v_i^{-1}(\mathcal H^r(f^\times G)|_Z)\cong v_i^{-1}F_Z$. Choose an etale cover $W_j\to Z$ on which $F_Z$ is a finite constant $A$-module sheaf. Then the family $W_j\times_Z(Z\times_XU_i)\to Z$ covers $Z$ and trivializes $\mathcal H^r(f^\times G)|_Z$ as those same finite constant $A$-modules, using [lem-kun-pullback-constant]. Thus its restriction to $Z$ is locally constant with finite stalks. Thus $f^\times G$ is bounded constructible by [def-weil-pbc-constructible-complexes], in precisely $[a-2d,b-2d]$. No finiteness of the trivializing covering family is needed: the stratification itself is finite. Finally [lem-sf-proetale-constructible-origin] and [lem-sf-comparison-pullback-exact] take this conclusion along $\nu_X^*$ to $Rf^!M$. This proves clause (1).

source.place: Proof, Step 1 (constructibility and the signed interval shift)

proof.text: Now let $K\in D^b_{ctf}(Y,A)$ have Tor amplitude in $[a,b]$, and choose a bounded constructible etale representative $G$ as in step 2. By [lem-sf-comparison-tor-amplitude](ii), $G$ has Tor amplitude in $[a,b]$ on the etale site. Put $\kappa=A/(\varpi_E)$. Apply [lem-exc-residue-tor-test] to this bounded constructible etale $G$: the complex $G\otimes_A^L\kappa_Y$ has cohomology zero outside $[a,b]$. This is an etale-site use of the residue-field criterion; no criterion for arbitrary pro-etale sheaves is being asserted.

Let $H=f^\times G$, which is bounded constructible by step 5 applied to any cohomological bounding interval of $K$. Restrict $H\otimes_A^L\kappa_X$ to a trivializing $u=u_i$. Using step 4, [lem-kun-inverse-image-monoidal] for $u$ and $f$, [lem-kun-pullback-constant] for the constant residue-field sheaves, and the shift compatibility of [lem-kun-derived-tensor-triangulated], obtain
$$
 u^{-1}(H\otimes_A^L\kappa_X)
 \cong ((u^{-1}f^{-1}G)[2d])\otimes_A^L\kappa_U
 \cong (u^{-1}f^{-1}(G\otimes_A^L\kappa_Y))[2d].
$$
Both $u^{-1}$ and $f^{-1}$ are exact on module sheaves by [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact]. The cohomology formula of [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-bounded-below] and the signed shift formula of [lem-sp-derived-cohomology-shift] therefore identify degree $r$ of the last complex with
$$u^{-1}f^{-1}\mathcal H^{r+2d}(G\otimes_A^L\kappa_Y).$$
It vanishes for $r\notin[a-2d,b-2d]$ by step 6. Vanishing on the covering $\{U_i\}$ is vanishing of the sheaf, so $H\otimes_A^L\kappa_X$ has cohomology in $[a-2d,b-2d]$.

source.place: Proof, displayed residue-field tensor calculation and concluding paragraph; written after local trivialization

proof.text: Apply [lem-exc-residue-tor-test] to the bounded constructible etale $H$ of step 7. It has Tor amplitude in $[a-2d,b-2d]$. By [lem-sf-comparison-tor-amplitude](i), $\nu_X^*H\cong Rf^!K$ has that same Tor amplitude against all degree-zero pro-etale $A$-module sheaves. Step 5 already proves its bounded constructibility. By [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude], it lies in $D^b_{ctf}(X,A)$, proving clause (2). The shift in step 5 is exactly the signed choice $c_f^-=c_f^+=-2d$ of [def-weil-exceptional-adjoint-admissibility]. Together with the bounded-class adjunction of [cor-sf-ambient-adjoint-discharge], these are the constructible analogues asserted in the statement. The unrestricted ambient clause (1) and the coefficient-transport statements at $\mathcal O_E,E,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ are not consequences of this argument.

let $f:X\to Y$ be smooth separated of pure relative dimension $d$.
Then $f$ satisfies the
two preservation clauses of
[def-weil-exceptional-adjoint-admissibility], with
$c_f^-=c_f^+=-2d$ in the signed convention of that definition:

1. *constructibility.* For all integers $a\leq b$,
$$
L\in D_c^{[a,b]}(Y,A)\quad\Longrightarrow\quad

$$

Thus every smooth morphism is
exceptional-adjoint admissible at $A=A_{E,n}$ in the constructible sense:
the preservation clauses of [def-weil-exceptional-adjoint-admissibility]
hold on the complexes of the blueprint's coefficient class. The ambient

not assumed: on the bounded constructible and finite-Tor coefficients that
the two clauses quantify over it is the theorem
[cor-sf-ambient-adjoint-discharge]. The unrestricted clause (1) of
[def-weil-exceptional-adjoint-admissibility], on all pro-étale sheaves, is

proof.text:
By [cor-pur-dualizing-object-purity] the right adjoint $Rf^!$, whose
existence on the coefficients used here is the theorem
[cor-sf-ambient-adjoint-discharge], is
identified with $Lf^*(-)(d)[2d]$ on finite-Tor objects. For a
bounded constructible complex $L$ without finite Tor amplitude, use
the tensor formula on all ordinary etale complexes of
[thm-asd-smooth-tensor], the orientation at $\Lambda$ of
[thm-pur-diagonal-dualizing-object], and the comparison
[thm-sf-ambient-adjoint-class]. They give the same identification
for $L$; no site-perfectness of $L$ is assumed. The criterion below is
applied at the finite etale level and transported to the small pro-etale
site along [thm-cbc-finite-level-proetale], as elsewhere in this
chapter.
Step 1: (1). The inverse image of [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-exact] is exact.
It preserves constructibility: pull back each finite stratification
and each finite locally constant sheaf on its strata, as in
[def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility]. Thus for
$L\in D_c^{[a,b]}(Y,A)$ the complex $Lf^*L$ is bounded constructible
with $\mathcal H^r(Lf^*L)\cong f^*\mathcal H^r(L)$, which vanishes for
$r\notin[a,b]$; the [def-coefficient-twists-detailed] twist preserves the
vanishing degrees by [prop-weil-twist-preserves], and the shift moves them, by the convention
$\mathcal H^r(C[2d])=\mathcal H^{r+2d}(C)$, to $[a-2d,b-2d]$.
Step 2: (2). Test the finite Tor amplitude of $Rf^!K$ by the residue
field criterion of [lem-exc-residue-tor-test]: it is equivalent to
the complex $\mathcal H^\bullet\bigl(Rf^!K\otimes^L_A\kappa\bigr)$ being
concentrated in $[a-2d,b-2d]$. Substituting the purity
identification and the associativity of the derived tensor product,

$$
Rf^!K\otimes^L_A\kappa
\;\cong\;\bigl(Lf^*K\otimes^L_A\kappa\bigr)(d)[2d]
\;\cong\;Lf^*\bigl(K\otimes^L_A\kappa\bigr)(d)[2d].
$$

By the same criterion applied to $K$, the complex
$K\otimes^L_A\kappa$ has cohomology in $[a,b]$; the inverse image
$Lf^*$ is exact, so $Lf^*(K\otimes^L_A\kappa)$ has cohomology in
$[a,b]$, and the twist by the locally constant free rank-one sheaf
$\Lambda(d)$ preserves the vanishing degrees. The shift therefore puts
the cohomology in $[a-2d,b-2d]$, which is the assertion. At field
coefficients the assertion is the case already recorded in
[lem-weil-field-tor-amplitude].
